title: A run whose parent died is closed, not stuck running forever
name: A run whose parent died is closed, not
description:
Seen 2026-09-15: `run` on core-runs-git-in-english-so-its-error-te-tljx started the agent (run d92w, pid 55417), then the host app was restarted and the `sober mcp` process that owned the run died with it. The agent died too, but nobody called `finishRun`: the record in .sober/local/runs/<id>.json keeps `exit: null` and `endedAt: null`, so `statusOf` says the node is running. `run` then refuses ('is running, so it cannot start') and `stop` says 'had already ended' — `stopRun` in packages/core/src/dispatch.ts:272 sees `process.kill` throw ESRCH, clears the pid file and returns false without writing the run's end. Nothing in the tools or the CLI can move the node again; the only way out is editing the record by hand, which is exactly what the skills forbid.

The pid file in packages/core/src/local.ts is already documented as 'a stale one is treated as no run at all', but the run record never learns that. Fix in core, in one place, so every surface inherits it: a run whose `exit` is null and whose pid is gone (no pid file, or `process.kill(pid, 0)` throws) is orphaned. Decide where that check lives — the cheapest is in `stopRun`: when the kill throws, call `finishRun` with `{ exit: 'failed', error: 'the process that owned this run is gone' }` plus `unjudged(...)` for the acceptance, so `stop` on an orphan closes it and `run` can start again. Consider also having `statusOf`/`loadBoard` treat such a run as failed on read, so the board never shows 'running' for a dead process — but keep the write in one place. `stop` in packages/mcp/src/tools/build.ts and the CLI's stop then say 'was already gone and is now recorded as failed' rather than 'had already ended'. One test in packages/core/src/dispatch.test.ts (or beside the existing run tests): write a run record with `exit: null` and a pid file naming a pid that does not exist, call `stopRun`, assert the record now has `exit: 'failed'`, an error naming the dead process, and that `statusOf` no longer says running. Worktree and branch stay untouched, as with any failure.

brief.approach:
One write, in one place, so every surface inherits it. Score 4: two files of real logic, the shape is already there in `stopRun`, and the test is a fixture with a dead pid.

**Where.** `stopRun` in `packages/core/src/dispatch.ts:272` already has the branch. `process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM')` throws `ESRCH`, the catch clears the stopped marker and the pid file, and returns `false` — and the run record keeps `exit: null` and `endedAt: null` forever, which is what makes `statusOf` say `running` (`packages/core/src/status.ts:43`, `isRunning(run)`), `run` refuse with "is running, so it cannot start", and `stop` say "had already ended". Nothing can move the node again.

In that catch, before returning, close the run:

```ts
await finishRun(paths, id, {
  exit: 'failed',
  error: 'the process that owned this run is gone',
  acceptance: (await unjudged(paths, node)).acceptance,
})
```

`finishRun` and `unjudged` are already imported at the top of the file (`./run.js` line 25, `./audit.js` line 3) and `dispatchNode` at line 193-195 is the existing call pair to copy — match its shape exactly rather than inventing a second one. `unjudged` takes the **node** id, not the run id; read it off the run record with `readRun`, which the file already uses, so `stopRun`'s signature does not change.

`finishRun` takes the writer lock (`withLock(paths, 'run', …)`). `stopRun` does not hold a lock, so there is no nesting — check that before writing, because a nested `withLock` on the same paths is a deadlock, not a bug you find in review.

**Return value.** `stopRun` still returns `false` for this path: nothing was killed, because nothing was alive. The callers say a different sentence off it:

- `packages/mcp/src/tools/build.ts:150-155` — the `false` branch today reads `${live[0]} had already ended.` It becomes a sentence that is true and actionable: the process that owned the run is gone and the run is now recorded as failed, so the node can be run again.
- The CLI's `stop` in `packages/cli/src/work.ts` — find it with `rg -n stopRun packages/cli/src` and change its false branch the same way, in the CLI's own register.

Do not change the `true` branch of either.

**Do not** teach `statusOf` or `loadBoard` to treat a dead pid as failed on read. The node's own text raises it and then says to keep the write in one place, and it is right: `statusOf` is pure over records and takes no `Paths`, so giving it a liveness probe would put a syscall inside the function every surface calls on every node. One write, in `stopRun`, reached by one command the person already types.

**The doc comment** on `stopRun` says "The stopping process does not write the run record — the process that owns the run does, when its child dies." That is now false in one case and the comment has to say so: when the owning process is gone, nobody will ever write it, so the stopper does — which is the whole defect.

**Test** in `packages/core/src/dispatch.test.ts`, beside the existing run tests. Build the state by hand rather than by killing a real process: `startRun` to get a record, `writeRunPid(paths, id, <a pid that does not exist>)` from `./local.js`, then `stopRun`. Assert three things — the record now has `exit: 'failed'` and an error naming the dead process, `statusOf` for that node is no longer `running`, and the run can be started again. For the dead pid, spawn a trivial child, await its exit, and reuse its pid: a hardcoded number can collide with a live process on the test machine, and this suite runs on three operating systems.

Nothing else changes. No new export from `core`, no schema change — `exit: 'failed'` and `error` are fields `Run` already has.

acceptance.proves: a run whose owning process is gone is closed as failed with an error naming the cause, the node stops reporting `running`, and the existing dispatch and run behaviour is unchanged

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'finishRun' -- packages/core/src/dispatch.ts && ! git grep -q 'process.kill' -- packages/core/src/status.ts packages/core/src/graph.ts
acceptance.proves: the write lives in `stopRun` alone — `statusOf` and the board read stayed pure over records and gained no liveness probe
the change is confined to core, the MCP stop tool and the CLI stop command — no schema, no dashboard, no other MCP tool
stopping a run that is genuinely alive still behaves as it did: the worktree is preserved and the record is written by the owning process
the two changed call sites compile against `stopRun`'s unchanged signature
